headline: UK and EU publish Brexit reset treaty texts
pages: The UK government and the EU on Thursday published the texts of two treaties agreed last week as part of a post-Brexit reset. They cover food trade and emissions trading, and were released with a bill to enact the deal. The food agreement has a 10-year termination clause. A party that ends it would have to pay reasonable and proportionate costs to rebuild border check infrastructure, which will be scaled back under the deal. Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch has said she would scrap the deal, and Reform UK's Nigel Farage has suggested he would refuse to pay. An internal analysis forecasts a 16% rise in exports of major farm commodities.
The UK will observe EU rules and attend some meetings, but will have no vote. The government says the deal cuts paperwork for food traders and protects exporters from carbon taxes. Source: BBC.
